rationale:
Evidence: iteration 10 (kp 1.3, kd 0.8, ki 0.5, base 0.9) is the best design so far at 735.0. Oval finishes 20/20 at 1.91 s, s-bend finishes 18/20 (progress 0.98), and slalom improved from 0.43 to 0.67 progress with 3/20 finishes. Max error is still pinned at the off-track limit (about 0.061 m), and steering oscillation stays moderate (0.27 to 0.33). Across iterations 4 to 10, each step that lowered kp and raised kd raised progress on the harder tracks. Slalom is the weakest track and the most likely model of the unseen final track.

Change: keep the iteration 10 geometry exactly, so the controller change is isolated. Lower kp from 1.3 to 1.15 to continue reducing proportional overshoot across the tape. Raise kd from 0.8 to 0.9 to keep the response damped as proportional action falls. Lower base_speed from 0.9 to 0.85 to give more turning margin on slalom's alternating curves. The cost is small: oval should still finish in about 2.0 s, which keeps the time term high. ki stays at 0.5, since the integral is not the limiting factor.

Expected result: slalom progress rises above 0.7 with fewer line-loss events, s-bend finish rate stays at or above 0.9, and oval stays at a 1.0 finish. Steering oscillation should remain at or below about 0.35.

Hypotheses: (H1) overshoot is still the main limit on slalom, so a further kp reduction with more kd raises slalom progress. (H2) if s-bend or oval progress drops, kp 1.15 is too weak to hold the line on curves, so the fallback is kp about 1.3 with kd 0.9. (H3) if slalom stays near 0.67, the limit is the response to alternating curvature, and the next lever is a narrower sensor spread (x = +/-0.03) or a lower base_speed.

Measurements wanted: progress, completion time and max_error per track, where max_error occurs, line_loss_events, steering_oscillation and control_effort, to separate overshoot from lag.
